Definition: from G303 and G3992; to send up or back:--send (again).
BiblicalUsage: The word means to send up, or to send back: Pilate, learning that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, sent Him to Herod — and Paul tells Philemon, 'Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels,' sending Onesimus back to his master. The same word sends a prisoner up to a higher court and sends a runaway slave back home with a letter.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for sending back carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two sendings — Jesus sent to Herod, and Onesimus sent back to Philemon as Paul's own heart.
